item.title: Pneumonia Detection on Chest X-Rays Derived from a U-Net Segmentation Model
item.description: arXiv:2611.09943v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pneumonia killed more than 740,000 children under the age of five in 2019, and it can be difficult to recognize on chest radiographs (CXRs): opacities may be faint in early disease, may sit behind the equally bright heart shadow, and may resemble other lung conditions. Most deep learning systems treat pneumonia detection as a yes-or-no classification task. This paper asks whether a model trained on a harder task, segmenting pneumonia pixel by pixel, can be turned into an effective detector for the simpler task of deciding whether an image contains pneumonia at all. The hypothesis is that the detailed supervision of segmentation forces the network to learn where and what the disease looks like, producing a better detector than training for detection alone. A U-Net was trained to segment pneumonia on the RSNA Pneumonia Detection Challenge dataset of 26,684 radiographs, whose rectangular bounding boxes were converted into pixel masks. The data are heavily imbalanced: 22.5% of images are positive, and only 2.6% of pixels fall inside a box, so focal loss with {\alpha} = 0.25 and {\gamma} = 2 and dropout were needed for the model to learn. On the harder segmentation task, the model reached a pixel-level F1 score of 0.45 on a held-out test set of 2,668 images. Applied to the simpler detection task, the same model reached a precision of 0.71, recall of 0.52, and F1 score of 0.60, with 91% specificity, and consistent scores on the development set. These results show that a segmentation-trained model transfers to detection while also showing where the suspected disease is. A direct comparison with a classifier trained only for detection on the same data is needed to confirm whether the segmentation-first approach is better, and is the main direction for future work.
item.dc:creator: Manasvini Singh

item.title: Benchmarking Neural Image Compression with DCT-Based Spectral Diagnostics
item.description: arXiv:2611.10000v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neural image compression (NIC) models are commonly evaluated with scalar rate-distortion metrics, which do not show how a codec treats individual spatial frequencies. We propose a benchmark that probes codecs with the DCT basis matrix and single-frequency test images. We measure relative off-target energy (leakage), the fraction of reconstruction energy outside the probed frequency, together with target-frequency gain. Exact decompositions and bounds relate these measurements to reconstruction error. At operating points nearest 1 bpp, the BMSHJ, MBT, and Cheng2020 models leave 80-97% of their reconstructed high-band energy outside the target bin and have target-frequency gains of 0.02-0.23, whereas TCM and FTIC attain off-target energy in the classical-codec range. Both probe types identify behavior absent from scalar metrics: released Cheng2020-Anchor models produce extreme pre-clamp outputs on isolated single-frequency inputs. Finally, decoder-only fine-tuning with natural-image and leakage losses reduces basis off-target energy by 90-99.8% across all eight evaluated architectures while keeping the bitstream fixed, at a Kodak PSNR cost of 0.09-0.59 dB.
item.dc:creator: Nikolay I. Kalmykov, Razan Dibo, Yujun Du, Yipeng Liu, Ivan Oseledets, Anh-Huy Phan

item.title: Covariate-Conditioned One-Step Diffusion for Multi-Horizon 3D Brain MRI Prediction in Aging and Neurodegeneration
item.description: arXiv:2611.10043v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Predicting longitudinal brain changes from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) can help characterize structural progression associated with aging and neurodegeneration. However, diffusion-based forecasting typically requires iterative denoising, limiting inference efficiency. We propose a covariate-conditioned one-step diffusion framework for multi-horizon prediction of 3D gray-matter density (GMD) maps. Rather than directly generating future anatomy, the model predicts longitudinal GMD changes through residual prediction in a single denoising step. The predicted changes are added to the baseline GMD map to reconstruct future anatomy. The model is conditioned on baseline anatomy, age, diagnosis, APOE4 allele count, and continuous follow-up time. Training combines mean squared error with a Pearson correlation loss to improve the spatial agreement between predicted and observed GMD changes. A unified model supports prediction horizons from 2 to 10 years. On the held-out ADNI test set, our method achieves a $\Delta$-Pearson of 0.478, mean squared error (MSE) of $5.176 \times 10^{-3}$, and structural similarity index measure (SSIM) of 0.979, with $\Delta$-Pearson reaching 0.582 at 10 years. Without retraining, external evaluation on AIBL yields a $\Delta$-Pearson of 0.450, MSE of $4.016 \times 10^{-3}$, and SSIM of 0.985. Ablation studies further demonstrate the benefits of residual prediction, covariate conditioning, and correlation-based supervision. Code: https://github.com/natenaile/OneStepBrainMRI.
item.dc:creator: Natenaile Asmamaw Shiferaw, Ali Farki, Deepika Koundal, Jussi Tohka

item.title: Frequency-consistent synthesis and selective transfer for medical image analysis
item.description: arXiv:2611.10070v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Complementary imaging is not always available, and realistic synthesis does not necessarily improve downstream analysis. Here we introduce a training framework linking medical image synthesis to task learning through adaptive frequency consistency and selective feature transfer. Image-specific frequency constraints encourage consistency of structure and detail. Features are transferred only when a teacher using synthetic images achieves a lower task-error score than the student by a task-specific margin on a labelled training sample. Evaluations across five datasets show improved translation fidelity with three adversarial and diffusion-based translators trained without paired supervision, alongside gains in brain-tumour segmentation on tumour-containing slices and lesion centre-point detection. All 105 reported paired comparisons yielded point estimates favouring the proposed methods, including 36 external translation comparisons on post?treatment MRI without retraining. These findings support synthetic modalities as task-oriented complements to acquired scans when complementary imaging is unavailable.
item.dc:creator: Zhuhui Wang, Jianwei Zuo, Xin Peng, Kai Zhong, Xuliang Deng, Jiajia Luo

item.title: Noise-Regularized Training for Learned Image Compression
item.description: arXiv:2611.10073v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Learned image compression (LIC) is trained almost exclusively on clean images: the only stochastic perturbation in the loop is an additive uniform proxy injected in the latent domain to keep the entropy model differentiable. Outside compression, by contrast, a long line of work---from Tikhonov regularization and contractive autoencoders through denoising score matching and modern diffusion models---has established that Gaussian noise at the input of a network with a clean target acts as a structured probe of the data manifold rather than as data augmentation. Building on this view, we introduce noise-regularized training for LIC: at every training step we add Gaussian noise to the encoder input while keeping the distortion target, the latent uniform proxy, the hyperprior, and the entropy coding pipeline unchanged. The recipe is architecture-agnostic and adds essentially no training or inference overhead. Across backbones and operating regimes it yields consistent BD-Rate gains: -2.60% on a reproduced ELIC and -0.85% / -1.05% / -2.38% on the Base/Medium/Large scales of a variable-rate DMCI codec, with DMCI-Large reaching -22.02% against VTM-22.0. A second-order expansion of the noisy RD loss accounts for these gains: because the noise enters upstream of the analysis transform, it converts the clean RD objective into a structured $O(\sigma^{2})$ regularizer comprising an information-weighted encoder-Jacobian penalty (rate side) and a Frobenius contractive penalty on the end-to-end reconstruction map (distortion side). A finite-difference Lipschitz analysis shows corresponding sensitivity reductions of ~12% for the encoder and ~8% for the end-to-end codec, while an exact-JVP test further shows preferential contraction of high-information directions. Code and trained models are available at https://github.com/Googolxx/NoiseRegu-LIC.
item.dc:creator: Renjie Zou, Zhiwei Huang, Dong Jiang

item.title: Polarization Aware Deep Learning Framework for SAR Despeckling
item.description: arXiv:2611.10091v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Speckle is an inherent characteristic of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery that complicates image interpretation and the extraction of reliable information. Although deep-learning-based despeckling methods have demonstrated promising performance, their applicability across different polarimetric configurations is often limited by the need for specialized architectures or separate training procedures. This paper presents a unified deep-learning framework for despeckling single-, dual-, and full-polarization SAR data using a single trained convolutional neural network. The proposed approach adopts a common nine-channel representation of the polarimetric covariance matrix and a polarization-aware masking strategy to accommodate different configurations without modifying the network architecture. Qualitative and quantitative comparison on three different scenes from different sensors demonstrate competitive performance across the considered experiments and support the feasibility of a unified, polarization-flexible approach to SAR despeckling across different polarimetric configurations.
item.dc:creator: Gianpaolo Passarello, Sergio Vitale, Hossein Aghababei, Giampaolo Ferraioli, Vito Pascazio

item.title: Dataset Collections: Challenges of Large-Scale Data Aggregation in 3D Medical Image Datasets
item.description: arXiv:2611.10144v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The development of deep learning-based medical AI depends on high-quality annotated data. Yet, dataset creation remains constrained by the need for expert radiologist annotations, limiting curated datasets to relatively small cohorts. To overcome this limitation, recent efforts increasingly aggregate disparate public datasets into large-scale dataset collections. However, combining datasets at scale often obscures data provenance, introducing substantial risks of reuse propagation, unintended leakage, bias amplification and distorted data distributions. In this work, we study these problems on a massive collection of 565k 3D radiological images across 1034 public datasets and provide practical resources to address them. Firstly, we formalize dataset collections as a distinct paradigm in medical image analysis and characterize their structural challenges, including reuse propagation, duplication, and provenance fragmentation. Secondly, we perform a large-scale empirical study of duplication on this collection and demonstrate extensive exact and near-duplicate reuse across public datasets via perceptual hashing and manual tracing, identifying a lower bound of 118k duplicate pairs. We make the perceptual hashes publicly accessible for comparison through our website, providing researchers with a standardized reference for identifying potential overlaps and shared provenance. Thirdly, since hashing alone cannot detect all duplicates, we introduce MAP (Metadata for Aggregation and Provenance), a lightweight, portable metadata profile for documenting provenance, known overlaps, and deduplication decisions in dataset collections. Our contributions help dataset collections shift from coarse aggregations to reliable and provenance-aware data scaling mechanisms in medical image analysis. A web tool supporting our work is available at https://mic-dct.dkfz.de/.

item.title: Kinematic Total-Body PET Video Reconstruction via Hierarchical List-Mode EM and Validation-Adaptive Space-Time Regularisation
item.description: arXiv:2611.11052v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Kinematic PET is introduced as an imaging task focused on visualisation of early radiotracer delivery and rapid multi-organ motion without gating. The proposed kinematic video reconstruction method uses 33-ms frames (~30 frames per second), initialised with 3D expectation maximisation (EM) time of flight (TOF) list-mode reconstruction, followed by cycles of a 2-stage update. These 2 stages are i) a hierarchical EM (HEM) update using multiple temporal pooling levels, and ii) a validation-adaptive space-time (VAST) regularisation update. HEM combines frame-specific EM corrections with corrections estimated from higher-count temporal blocks, slowing noise amplification for the ultrashort frames. VAST mixes each 3D target patch in a frame with source patches sampled nearby in space and time. It selects the candidate that best matches the mean of the corresponding patches in the two adjacent frames, with the unchanged patch also eligible. Optional temporal block sum correction uses the initial EM temporal sum as a reference to reduce loss of spatial detail. HEM+VAST was evaluated with a dynamic digital phantom, and demonstrated on human FDG data acquired on a Siemens Biograph Vision Quadra (28 - 58 s post-injection). At a background spatial coefficient of variation of 10%, the temporal full width at half maximum of the fastest phantom bolus was 151 ms with HEM+VAST, compared with 86 ms for the ground truth. The video frame rate FDG images reveal vascular and organ detail, radiotracer bolus passage and respiration-related multi-organ motion. Kinematic PET could complement conventional dynamic PET by supporting the development of image-derived physiological biomarkers and motion estimation for quantitative reconstruction. Future work should compare HEM+VAST with prior 4D PET reconstruction methods at the same 33-ms frame duration and matched noise levels.
item.dc:creator: Andrew J. Reader, Gary J. R. Cook, Paul K. Marsden, Sarah-May Gould, Alexander Hammers, Simon R. Cherry

item.title: Leveraging High-Activity Post-Therapeutic I-131 Scans for Deep Learning Reconstruction of Extremely Sparse Planar Images in Differentiated Thyroid Cancer
item.description: arXiv:2611.12044v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Background: Diagnostic I-131 whole-body planar imaging in differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC) is count-limited by low administered activity, and quality worsens under rapid acquisition. Models trained on such data struggle because their targets lack photon statistics. Purpose: To test whether high-quality post-therapeutic (PT) I-131 scans can serve as superior training references for enhancing sparse diagnostic planar images, using transfer learning and input-image addition. Methods: In this single-center prospective study, 111 patients were enrolled in PT training (n = 19), diagnostic follow-up (FU) training (n = 58), and FU paired test (n = 34) cohorts. Five Restormer-based models were trained: FU_DLx2 on FU labels; PT_DLx2 transfer-learned on PT data; PT_DLx1+ and PT_DLx2+ with input-image addition; PT_DLx6 as a PT-only reference. Test-time processing used two-step denormalization and Poisson re-scaling to preserve noise statistics. Quality was assessed by PSNR, SSIM, and a blinded dual-reader evaluation of all 34 test-cohort patients. Results: PT_DLx2 achieved the highest PSNR (34.4 +/- 3.6 dB) and SSIM (0.81 +/- 0.07). PT_DLx1+ and PT_DLx2+ were comparable (33.8 and 33.3 dB; SSIM 0.80). FU_DLx2 ranked below the unprocessed fast scan (30.3 vs. 32.0 dB; 0.76 vs. 0.79). Subjectively, PT_DLx2+ scored highest in image quality (4.54 +/- 0.60) and diagnostic confidence (4.54 +/- 0.60), surpassing the reference standard (4.19 +/- 0.83 and 4.31 +/- 0.81; P = 0.005 and P = 0.008). FU_DLx2 and PT_DLx6 scored lowest. Conclusion: Count-rich PT scans provide effective training priors for reconstructing extremely sparse images. Input-image addition and cross-domain transfer learning from PT data outperformed direct training on count-limited diagnostic data, supporting 2x scan acceleration with quality matching or exceeding the unaccelerated standard scan for selected PT-derived configurations.
item.dc:creator: Boyang Pan, Hang Yang, Jianchen Pan, Cui Gan, Lanxi Zhang, Hongmin Li, Nan-Jie Gong

item.title: Next-Generation Segmentation in Radiotherapy: A Narrative Review from Atlas-Based Methods to Agentic Vision-Language Models
item.description: arXiv:2611.12085v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Precise segmentation of target volumes and organs at risk is an essential prerequisite for modern, high-precision radiation therapy. However, this task has traditionally been time-consuming and subject to high interobserver variability. Motivated by these limitations, more advanced and novel approaches to automating this task have been developed over the past two decades. This narrative review highlights representative milestones, with a focus on the most recent developments. These approaches include atlas-based label propagation, convolutional architectures, promptable foundation models, and, most recently, vision-language models (VLMs), which integrate clinical text with volumetric segmentation. Each methodological generation has addressed limitations of its predecessor while introducing new ones. A substantial gap remains between research progress and clinical deployment, as routine workflows continue to be dominated by atlas-based and narrow task-specific deep-learning tools, which remain strong baselines in geometric overlap metrics but are highly rigid in terms of application, versatility, portability, and interpretability. As contouring systems further grow in complexity, conventional geometric overlap metrics become insufficient, motivating evaluation paradigms that incorporate surface-based, dosimetric, and prompt-adherence assessment. Emerging agentic architectures that combine large language models, retrieval-augmented generation, and vision-language segmentation modules are leading towards more flexible, guideline-aware, interactive contouring workflows. These systems could automate flexible and interpretable knowledge-based contouring and actively support the clinical reasoning underlying target volume definition.
item.dc:creator: Josef A. Buchner, Richard Osuala, Ayhan Can Erdur, Melissa C. Olufs, Stephanie E. Combs, Jan C. Peeken

item.title: A four-step validation protocol for radiomic survival analysis in small cohorts: a body composition case study
item.description: arXiv:2611.12682v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (GEP-NET) lack prognostic biomarkers, and computed tomography (CT)-based body composition radiomics at the third lumbar vertebra (L3) is a promising candidate. Small cohorts make high-dimensional radiomic models prone to overfitting and single-split evaluations variable and optimistic. This methodological study proposes a four-step validation protocol for radiomic survival analysis in small cohorts: (1) false discovery rate (FDR)-corrected feature selection, (2) a dual-path comparison of prior feature selection versus embedded regularization, (3) repeated nested cross-validation (CV) and (4) a negative control with Gaussian noise features. In 78 GEP-NET patients, 535 radiomic features from five L3 compartments were used to evaluate five survival models with Harrell's concordance index (C-index), time-dependent area under the curve (AUC) and integrated Brier score (IBS). Step 1 selected at least one feature in 18% of outer folds under noise (nominal level 20%) versus 84% with radiomic features. The dual-path comparison showed no consistent difference between strategies. Repeated nested CV reduced variability across seeds (41% median reduction in C-index standard deviation), but not enough to distinguish models. The nested CV C-index exceeded chance by 0.07-0.15 with radiomic features but not clearly under noise (0.40-0.42 with prior feature selection, 0.47-0.55 with embedded regularization). Frequently selected features tentatively linked greater subcutaneous fat, skeletal muscle compactness and texture to better prognosis. These findings suggest a modest prognostic signal in L3 radiomics, with considerable uncertainty that the protocol quantifies. The protocol may transfer to other small-cohort radiomic survival studies. Code: https://github.com/marielatalaveram/radiomics-survival-validation-protocol.
item.dc:creator: Mariela Talavera-Mu\~noz, Cecilia Diana-Albelda, Miguel Antonio Sampedro-Nu\~nez, Victor Rodriguez-Laval, Jesus Bescos, \'Alvaro Garc\'ia-Mart\'in

item.title: From Discrete Snapshots to Geometric Entity: Motion-Native Channel Tracking for THz Near-Field XL-MIMO
item.description: arXiv:2611.10587v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Channel tracking in mobile terahertz (THz) near-field extremely large-scale multiple-input multiple-output (XL-MIMO) systems is challenging because spherical-wave propagation couples angle and range, leading to rapid and nonlinear channel evolution under sparse pilot observations. Existing approaches typically estimate pilot-local channel or position snapshots before applying temporal tracking or smoothing, making them vulnerable to information loss during snapshot formation. To break this bottleneck, we propose a paradigm shift from tracking discrete snapshots to estimating a holistic geometric entity, namely, one shared continuous UE trajectory over the tracking window. Specifically, we parameterize the trajectory using a low-dimensional cubic B-spline representation and directly couple the per-pilot profile likelihoods through this shared trajectory before any pilot-local position estimate is finalized, thereby inducing continuous near-field channel evolution. We further characterize the efficient geometric information supplied by each pilot observation and its aggregation in the shared spline-coefficient space. Based on this formulation, we develop a regularized maximum a posteriori estimator and a quadratic-penalty lifted solver that separates parallel pilot-local geometric updates from a structured global spline update. The resulting global system is banded and, for a fixed spline degree, admits linear-complexity factorization, enabling an efficient structured implementation. Simulations demonstrate consistently improved tracking accuracy over representative temporally refined baselines in the tested medium-to-high-SNR regime, together with a favorable accuracy--runtime trade-off. These results highlight the benefit of coupling sparse pilot observations through a shared continuous trajectory rather than temporally processing independently estimated snapshots.
item.dc:creator: Yuheng Fan, Chuang Yang, Mugen Peng

item.title: Differentiable Inverse Rendering Recovers Intrinsic Properties from Intravascular Optical Coherence Tomography
item.description: arXiv:2611.12686v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Medical images encode intrinsic tissue properties that indicate disease progression, yet these properties remain entangled with the system-dependent physics of image formation. Differentiable inverse rendering asks whether they are recoverable by inverting the imaging system's forward physics rather than through post-hoc correction. We address this in optical coherence tomography (OCT), focusing on the optical attenuation coefficient, a per-pixel marker of pathology and cellular composition. Conventional recovery relies on closed-form inversions limited to simplified light-tissue models, or learned methods coupled to specific imaging configurations. We instead recover per-pixel attenuation from a single OCT image by gradient descent through a differentiable physics-based forward model. We verified the method against analytical solutions, validated it on five in vitro phantoms, and applied it without modification to 29{,}269 clinical intravascular OCT images from 128 patients. The inversion needs no training data or segmentations and is portable across platforms and retrospective archives. Replacing the forward model or recovering another optical parameter leaves the optimization procedure unchanged. We demonstrate per-pixel recovery is tractable because gradient information scales to this high-dimensional problem, where gradient-free methods become intractable. Our work supports quantitative tissue characterization from OCT images and provides a framework for extension across imaging modalities and organ systems.
item.dc:creator: Ajay Manicka, Karim Kadry, Sebastian Ruiz-Lopera, Maryam Alsharqi, Sanjana Arji, Samuel Ruiperez-Campillo, Nestor Uribe-Patarroyo, Brett E. Bouma, Farhad Nezami, Elazer R. Edelman

item.title: U-WNO:U-Net-enhanced Wavelet Neural Operator for fetal head segmentation
item.description: arXiv:2411.16890v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This article describes the development of a novel U-Net-enhanced Wavelet Neural Operator (U-WNO),which combines wavelet decomposition, operator learning, and an encoder-decoder mechanism. This approach harnesses the superiority of the wavelets in time frequency localization of the functions, and the combine down-sampling and up-sampling operations to generate the segmentation map to enable accurate tracking of patterns in spatial domain and effective learning of the functional mappings to perform regional segmentation. By bridging the gap between theoretical advancements and practical applications, the U-WNO holds potential for significant impact in multiple science and industrial fields, facilitating more accurate decision-making and improved operational efficiencies. The operator is demonstrated for different pregnancy trimesters, utilizing two-dimensional ultrasound images.
item.dc:creator: Pranava Seth, Deepak Mishra, Veena Iyer

item.title: JND-Guided Light-Weight Neural Pre-Filter for Perceptual Image Coding
item.description: arXiv:2510.10648v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Just Noticeable Distortion (JND)-guided pre-filter is a promising technique for improving the perceptual compression efficiency of image coding. However, existing methods are often computationally expensive, and the field lacks standardized benchmarks for fair comparison. To address these challenges, this paper introduces a twofold contribution. First, we develop and open-source FJNDF-Pytorch, a unified benchmark for frequency-domain JND-Guided pre-filters. Second, leveraging this platform, we propose a complete learning framework for a novel, lightweight Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method achieves state-of-the-art compression efficiency, consistently outperforming competitors across multiple datasets and encoders. In terms of computational cost, our model is exceptionally lightweight, requiring only 7.15 GFLOPs to process a 1080p image, which is merely 14.1% of the cost of recent lightweight network. Our work presents a robust, state-of-the-art solution that excels in both performance and efficiency, supported by a reproducible research platform. The open-source implementation is available at https://github.com/viplab-fudan/FJNDF-Pytorch.
item.dc:creator: Yangyang Wu, Chenlong He, Yuanheng Chen, Yibo Fan

item.title: Triple-Phase Sequential Fusion Network with Contrast Enhancement Kinetics for Hepatobiliary-Phase Liver MRI Synthesis
item.description: arXiv:2604.22904v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Gadoxetate disodium-enhanced MRI is essential for the detection and characterization of hepatocellular carcinoma. However, acquisition of the hepatobiliary phase (HBP) requires a prolonged post-contrast delay, which reduces workflow efficiency and increases the risk of motion artifacts. In this study, we propose a Triple-Phase Sequential Fusion Network (TriPF-Net) with contrast enhancement kinetics to synthesize HBP images by leveraging the sequential information from pre-HBP sequences: while T1-weighted imaging serves as the indispensable baseline, the model adaptively integrates arterial-phase (AP) and venous-phase (VP) features when available. By modeling the tissue-specific contrast uptake and excretion dynamics across these three phases, TriPF-Net ensures robust HBP synthesis even under the stochastic absence of one or both dynamic contrast-enhanced sequences. In addition, clinical variables, including age, sex, total bilirubin, and albumin, are incorporated to enhance physiological consistency. Compared with conventional methods, TriPF-Net achieved superior performance on datasets from two centers. On the first-center dataset, the model achieved an MAE of 10.65, a PSNR of 23.27, and an SSIM of 0.76. On the second-center dataset, the model was trained independently, and the corresponding values were 12.41, 23.11, and 0.78, respectively. Moreover, lesion-level evaluation showed that the synthesized images achieved contrast comparable to that of real HBP images, with no significant difference in CNR (P = 0.2699). Blinded evaluations confirmed synthesized images were visually comparable to real HBP, with TriPF-Net remaining robust to missing input phases. This flexible solution enhances clinical workflow and lesion depiction, and may also serve as an automated quality control reference to flag real HBP acquisitions that warrant closer inspection.
item.dc:creator: Qiuli Wang, Xinhuan Sun, Fengxi Chen, Yongxu Liu, Jie Cheng, Lin Chen, Jiafei Chen, Siwei Miao, Xingpeng Zhang, Yue Zhang, Xiaoming Li, Wei Chen

item.title: FlowFPR: Flow Matching Prior for Oversampled Fourier Phase Retrieval
item.description: arXiv:2611.00157v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Fourier phase retrieval aims to reconstruct images from magnitude-only measurements; however, the absence of phase information, noises, and channel ambiguities make the recovery of natural color images challenging. Although diffusion-prior-based methods impose strong image constraints, their recovery performance degrades under higher measurement noise, and repeated generative updates incur substantial computational overhead. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a novel method, termed FlowFPR, that integrates a pretrained flow-matching prior with the relaxed averaged alternating reflections (RAAR) algorithm for oversampled Fourier phase retrieval. In the basic version of FlowPR (Flow-RAAR-basic), a color image is estimated by repeatedly performing four steps at each outer iteration, where the flow-prior prediction step exploits single-step straight-line prediction, considerably reducing the generation cost. Nevertheless, Flow-RAAR-basic still suffers from two critical issues: (i) the predefined fusion weights, \(\lambda_n\), might lead to either ineffective or excessive correction, and (ii) the fixed iteration number used by RAAR algorithm does not allow adaptation to measurement noise. To address these two issues, we develop two improved algorithms, Flow-RAAR-adaptive and Flow-RAAR-controlled, respectively. Moreover, these two improved algorithms naturally lead to a joint variant, Flow-RAAR-joint, which combines their advantages. Extensive experiments on a natural face image dataset demonstrate the superior performance of the four proposed methods compared with other relevant competing methods, as well as their acceleration over two recent diffusion-based methods. In the noise setting, Flow-RAAR-joint performs best among the four proposed methods.
item.dc:creator: Li Jiatai, Cao Wenfei, Chen Yang, Miao Kun

item.title: LFX: Fusion-Form-Flexible Light Field Modeling for Dense Semantic Segmentation and Salient Object Detection
item.description: arXiv:2503.00747v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Two distinct light field (LF) observation forms, namely sub-aperture images (S.Aperture images) and focal stack (FS), correspond to two fusion settings: the central image with S.Aperture images (CS) and the central image with FS (CF). Existing LF perception methods are typically form-specific, while a modeling design that can be separately instantiated under either setting remains underexplored. To address this gap, we present LFX, a form-flexible LF perception framework. Here, ``X'' represents the LF observation form, indicating that the one modeling design can be separately instantiated under two fusion settings (CS and CF). Specifically, we propose Field-of-Parallax Angular Subspace Modeling (FoP-ASM), which maps the feature difference between each auxiliary observation and the central image to an observation-specific angular marker. This avoids pairwise modeling among auxiliary observations and form-specific geometric assumptions. Meanwhile, a shared manifold subspace and the associated regularization losses constrain the angular residuals within a common feature space, promoting semantic consistency across auxiliary observations. Extensive evaluations across three LF datasets show that LFX achieves state-of-the-art results across distinct LF forms. Under the S.Aperture images and FS settings, respectively, LFX reduces MAE by 12.12%/20.59% on DUTLF-V2 and by 6.15%/7.69% on HFUT, while achieving the best performance on UrbanLF-real. The source code will be made publicly available at https://github.com/FeiT-FeiTeng/LFX.
item.dc:creator: Fei Teng, Lingxin Huang, Buyin Deng, Kai Luo, Boyuan Zheng, Zheng Fang, Hong Zheng, Kunyu Peng, Jiaming Zhang, Yaonan Wang, Kailun Yang

item.title: EgoEV-HandPose: Egocentric 3D Hand Pose Estimation and Gesture Recognition with Stereo Event Cameras
item.description: arXiv:2605.12297v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Egocentric 3D hand pose estimation and gesture recognition are fundamental to understanding hand interactions from first-person observations. Robust perception remains challenging: frame-based cameras suffer from motion blur and limited dynamic range, while event-based approaches face ego-motion interference, monocular depth ambiguity, and limited real-world datasets. We propose EgoEV-HandPose, an end-to-end framework for joint 3D bimanual hand pose estimation and gesture recognition from stereo event streams. Its core module, KeypointBEV, combines sparse 3D joint hypotheses with geometry-aware stereo fusion and iterative reprojection-guided refinement to progressively resolve depth uncertainty and improve pose accuracy. We also introduce EgoEVHands, the first large-scale real-world stereo event dataset for egocentric 3D bimanual hand pose estimation and gesture recognition. Built upon EgoEvGesture recordings, it adds dense 2D/3D hand annotations and comprises 2,498 annotated stereo sequence pairs across 38 gesture classes. Extensive experiments demonstrate that EgoEV-HandPose achieves state-of-the-art performance on EgoEVHands, obtaining a mean per-joint position error (MPJPE) of 30.54mm and a gesture recognition accuracy of 86.87%, significantly outperforming RGB-based stereo and previous event-based methods. The framework exhibits exceptional robustness under low illumination and severe bimanual occlusion. Experiments on DHP19 further demonstrate the cross-dataset and cross-architecture generalizability of the KeypointBEV refinement design. Dataset and code will be released at https://github.com/ZJUWang01/EgoEV-HandPose.

item.title: Human-in-the-Loop Signature Bootstrapping for UAV Hyperspectral PFM-1 Mine Detection
item.description: arXiv:2607.25310v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) is useful for material discrimination, but operational mine screening also depends on how many false alarms must be inspected before targets are found. This paper studies PFM-1 landmine detection in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) visible and near-infrared (VNIR) HSI using spectral angle mapper (SAM), matched filter (MF), adaptive coherence estimator (ACE), and constrained energy minimization (CEM). We compare a ground-measured SVC signature, a fully informed in-scene core-pixel signature, and a simulated human-in-the-loop signature bootstrap. Besides receiver operating characteristic area under the curve and average precision, we report target-discovery curves and spatial candidate-review counts. Full-review bootstrapping reaches the fully informed in-scene signature case after all seven target regions are verified, but the required inspection effort varies strongly: ACE confirms all regions in two rounds and nine candidate inspections, whereas the SAM variants need thousands of candidate reviews for their final target locations. Code is available at https://github.com/SagarLekhak/IEEE_WHISPERS_2026_UAV_HSI_PFM1.
item.dc:creator: Sagar Lekhak, Prasanna Reddy Pulakurthi, Emmett J. Ientilucci
